tagline: The older Las Vegas, from a Mormon fort to a tower.
intro: The byway starts at Washington Avenue by the Old Mormon Fort and runs south down Las Vegas Boulevard, past the Neon Museum and the downtown casinos around Fremont Street, to Sahara Avenue near the Strat. It is under three and a half miles, and the Federal Highway Administration calls it a work of art at night.

South of downtown the boulevard is lined with the older motels, bars and wedding chapels of the Vegas that came before the megaresorts. Many of the signs over them date from the 1950s, the heyday of neon.

moments.title: Old Las Vegas Mormon Fort
moments.text: Mormon missionaries finished it in 1855 as a midpoint between Salt Lake City and Los Angeles. It was the first building in a town that arrived fifty years later.

moments.title: Neon Museum
moments.text: More than 200 old signs from casinos and other businesses stand outdoors here, and the visitor center is the lobby of the La Concha Motel, moved over from the Strip in 2006.

moments.title: The Strat
moments.text: Bob Stupak started with plans for a giant neon sign. It became an observation tower, and when he asked to take it to 1,825 feet the city stopped him at 1,149.
